quests.question: Our office is located on ___ fourth floor of that building.
quests.sentence: Our office is located on ___ fourth floor of that building.
quests.hint: This number identifies a specific position among the floors in the building.
quests.explanation: Ordinal numbers like 'fourth' identify a position within an existing, known sequence, so they take 'the' — 'the fourth floor' means the floor in that specific position.

quests.question: We're planning to open ___ fourth store in the downtown area next year.
quests.sentence: We're planning to open ___ fourth store in the downtown area next year.
quests.hint: Here 'fourth' is really just counting a new addition, not identifying a position in a known list.
quests.explanation: When 'fourth' simply means 'one more, making four total' rather than identifying a specific position in an existing sequence, it works like a regular counting adjective and takes 'a' — 'a fourth store', similar to 'another store'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: This is ___ third time this printer has jammed today.
quests.sentence: This is ___ third time this printer has jammed today.
quests.hint: This number is identifying a position in a count you're tracking.
quests.explanation: Just like 'the fourth floor', this ordinal identifies a specific position — the third occurrence in a series you're counting — so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: That was hands-down ___ funniest movie I've seen all year.
quests.sentence: That was hands-down ___ funniest movie I've seen all year.
quests.hint: This adjective is being compared against every other movie you've seen.
quests.explanation: Superlatives like 'funniest' compare one thing against an entire group and always take 'the'.

quests.question: It's ___ funny movie, but not really the best one out there.
quests.sentence: It's ___ funny movie, but not really the best one out there.
quests.hint: This time, the adjective isn't comparing it to anything — it's just a plain description.
quests.explanation: 'Funny' here is a simple, non-comparative description, not a superlative, so it takes 'a' — 'funny' begins with a consonant sound. Compare this with 'the funniest', which ranks it above every other movie.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: She was named ___ most valuable player of the tournament.
quests.sentence: She was named ___ most valuable player of the tournament.
quests.hint: This title ranks her above everyone else in the tournament.
quests.explanation: 'Most valuable' is a superlative phrase, so it takes 'the', following the same pattern as 'the funniest movie'.

quests.question: Please turn to ___ next page for further instructions.
quests.sentence: Please turn to ___ next page for further instructions.
quests.hint: This identifies one specific page in a known sequence.
quests.explanation: 'The next page' identifies a specific position in an established sequence of pages, so it takes 'the', much like an ordinal number.

quests.question: If you can't make this flight, I can book you on ___ later flight instead.
quests.sentence: If you can't make this flight, I can book you on ___ later flight instead.
quests.hint: This isn't one specific, identified flight — it's simply some other, unspecified option.
quests.explanation: 'A later flight' introduces an unspecified alternative, not one particular identified flight, so it takes 'a'. Compare this with 'the next page', which points to one specific, known item in a sequence.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: This is ___ final round of interviews before we make a decision.
quests.sentence: This is ___ final round of interviews before we make a decision.
quests.hint: This identifies the last position in a known sequence of interview rounds.
quests.explanation: 'The final round' identifies a specific position at the end of a known sequence, so it takes 'the', just like 'the next page' and 'the third time'.

quests.question: My daughter is still in ___ school — she won't be home until three.
quests.sentence: My daughter is still in ___ school — she won't be home until three.
quests.hint: This describes her role as a student, not the building itself.
quests.explanation: 'In school' here means attending classes as a student — a fixed institutional expression that takes no article, regardless of which building she's actually in.

quests.question: I need to stop by ___ school to pick up some paperwork from the office.
quests.sentence: I need to stop by ___ school to pick up some paperwork from the office.
quests.hint: This time, you're talking about visiting the actual building.
quests.explanation: Here 'school' refers to the specific physical building you're going to visit, not the institutional idea of attending classes, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: He's been in ___ hospital for two days after the surgery.
quests.sentence: He's been in ___ hospital for two days after the surgery.
quests.hint: This describes his situation as a patient, not the building.
quests.explanation: 'In hospital' describes the institutional situation of being a patient receiving care, so it takes no article, following the same pattern as 'in school'.

quests.question: This bakery makes ___ best croissants in the whole neighborhood.
quests.sentence: This bakery makes ___ best croissants in the whole neighborhood.
quests.hint: Think back to how superlatives are handled.
quests.explanation: 'Best' is a superlative comparing these croissants to every other bakery's, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: We're meeting again on ___ second Tuesday of next month.
quests.sentence: We're meeting again on ___ second Tuesday of next month.
quests.hint: This is a different kind of special number pattern from the last question — think about position in a sequence.
quests.explanation: 'The second Tuesday' identifies a specific position within the Tuesdays of that month, so it takes 'the', even though the underlying reasoning here is about ordinal position rather than superlative comparison.

quests.question: They're opening ___ fifth location this year, right here in our city.
quests.sentence: They're opening ___ fifth location this year, right here in our city.
quests.hint: Is this identifying one specific location in a known sequence, or just counting a new addition?
quests.explanation: Like 'a fourth store' from an earlier level, 'fifth' here just counts a new addition rather than identifying a position in an existing, known sequence, so it takes 'a'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: After the accident, she spent several weeks in ___ hospital recovering.
quests.sentence: After the accident, she spent several weeks in ___ hospital recovering.
quests.hint: This is about her situation as a patient, following the pattern from before.
quests.explanation: 'In hospital' again describes the institutional situation of being a patient, so it takes no article, the same reasoning used earlier.

quests.question: ___ hospital on Main Street just opened a new wing for children.
quests.sentence: ___ hospital on Main Street just opened a new wing for children.
quests.hint: This time, a specific building is being identified by its location.
quests.explanation: Here 'hospital' is identified as one particular building by its location on Main Street, so it takes 'the', not the institutional zero-article pattern.

quests.question: He spent five years in ___ prison before he was released early for good behavior.
quests.sentence: He spent five years in ___ prison before he was released early for good behavior.
quests.hint: This describes his situation as an inmate, following the same institutional pattern.
quests.explanation: 'In prison' describes an institutional situation, not a specific building, so it takes no article, just like 'in school' and 'in hospital'.

quests.question: We ended up ordering ___ same dish we had last time — it was that good.
quests.sentence: We ended up ordering ___ same dish we had last time — it was that good.
quests.hint: This special word always pairs with one particular article.
quests.explanation: 'The same' is a fixed expression that always takes 'the', regardless of what noun follows it.

quests.question: This time, let's try ___ different dish instead of ordering the same thing again.
quests.sentence: This time, let's try ___ different dish instead of ordering the same thing again.
quests.hint: This describes a new, unspecified choice, not something already established.
quests.explanation: 'A different dish' introduces a new, unspecified option, unlike 'the same dish', which points to something already known and fixed. 'Different' also begins with a consonant sound.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: You're ___ only person who noticed the mistake in the report.
quests.sentence: You're ___ only person who noticed the mistake in the report.
quests.hint: This word implies there's no one else — a strong form of uniqueness.
quests.explanation: 'The only' is a fixed expression marking unique reference — there's exactly one person this applies to, so it always takes 'the'.

quests.question: She's applying to ___ university with a strong engineering program.
quests.sentence: She's applying to ___ university with a strong engineering program.
quests.hint: Remember that 'u' doesn't always make a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: 'University' starts with a 'y' glide consonant sound, so it takes 'a', the same pattern taught in an earlier level.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: He works part-time at ___ art institute downtown.
quests.sentence: He works part-time at ___ art institute downtown.
quests.hint: This time, the word right after the gap really does start with a vowel sound.
quests.explanation: 'Art' begins with a genuine vowel sound, so it takes 'an', unlike 'university', which only looks like it should.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a vowel sound

quests.question: My brother is currently away at ___ college, studying biology.
quests.sentence: My brother is currently away at ___ college, studying biology.
quests.hint: This describes his situation as a student, following the institutional pattern.
quests.explanation: 'At college' describes the institutional situation of being a student, so it takes no article, the same reasoning used with school and hospital.

quests.question: This is officially ___ longest bridge in the entire country.
quests.sentence: This is officially ___ longest bridge in the entire country.
quests.hint: Think back to how superlatives work.
quests.explanation: 'Longest' is a superlative comparing this bridge to every other one in the country, so it takes 'the'.

quests.question: I heard they're building ___ second runway at the airport to handle more flights.
quests.sentence: I heard they're building ___ second runway at the airport to handle more flights.
quests.hint: Is this identifying a position in an existing sequence, or just adding a new one?
quests.explanation: Like 'a fourth store' and 'a fifth location' earlier, this 'second' just counts a new addition rather than identifying a position in an already-known sequence, so it takes 'a'.
quests.grammarRule: Indefinite article before a consonant sound

quests.question: My grandfather spent his whole career working at ___ same company downtown.
quests.sentence: My grandfather spent his whole career working at ___ same company downtown.
quests.hint: This fixed expression always pairs with the same article, no matter the context.
quests.explanation: 'The same' is a fixed expression, just as it was earlier with the dish example, and always takes 'the'.

quests.question: Even after ___ third attempt, the code still wouldn't compile correctly.
quests.sentence: Even after ___ third attempt, the code still wouldn't compile correctly.
quests.hint: This number identifies a specific position in a count.
quests.explanation: 'The third attempt' identifies a specific position in a sequence of tries, so it takes 'the', following the same ordinal pattern as earlier levels.

quests.question: By ___ time the ambulance reached the hospital, the patient was stable.
quests.sentence: By ___ time the ambulance reached the hospital, the patient was stable.
quests.hint: This is a fixed phrase meaning 'by the point when...'.
quests.explanation: 'By the time' is a fixed expression used to introduce when something happened relative to something else, and it always includes 'the'.

quests.question: After years of hard work, she finally graduated from ___ college with top honors.
quests.sentence: After years of hard work, she finally graduated from ___ college with top honors.
quests.hint: This describes completing her studies as part of an institution, not a specific building.
quests.explanation: 'Graduated from college' uses the institutional, zero-article sense of college, the same pattern used throughout this chapter with school, hospital, and prison.
